highlights:
# Wasabi Joins the Vultr Cloud Alliance to Deliver Greater Cloud Flexibility and Better Economics

2 min read September 29, 2026 0

Vultr today announced that Wasabi Technologies, a cloud object storage provider, has joined the Vultr Cloud Alliance, bringing together Vultr cloud infrastructure and Wasabi S3-compatible object storage to give organizations greater flexibility and better economics across compute and storage.

...

With Vultr and Wasabi, customers can run applications and workloads on Vultr while keeping data in Wasabi. Direct private connectivity between the two environments is designed to improve the economics of accessing Wasabi Object Storage from Vultr compute.

Wasabi provides predictable object storage pricing with no egress or API request fees. Vultr provides high-performance cloud compute with included bandwidth and predictable egress pricing, supported by direct connectivity to Wasabi. Together, customers get better economics across compute, storage, and data access as they scale.

...

For organizations already using Wasabi, the partnership provides a practical way to introduce Vultr compute without changing their existing storage strategy.

Applications running on Vultr Cloud Compute, Bare Metal, Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE), or Vultr Cloud GPU can use Wasabi as an S3-compatible object storage target. This creates a more composable approach to cloud infrastructure, giving organizations the choice to select and scale compute and storage independently based on the performance, capacity, and economics each workload requires.

The combination supports a broad range of data-intensive use cases, including backup and disaster recovery, long-term data retention, cloud applications, and the storage and processing of large media and content libraries. This flexibility also extends to AI, enabling organizations to store datasets and other AI data in Wasabi while using Vultr Cloud GPU and compute infrastructure to meet the performance and capacity their workloads require.

# SoftwareOne Joins the Vultr Cloud Alliance to Expand Enterprise Cloud Choice

3 min read September 16, 2026 0

SoftwareOne has joined the Vultr Cloud Alliance, bringing together Vultr’s enterprise cloud infrastructure with SoftwareOne’s expertise across cloud advisory, FinOps, migration, optimization, and managed services.

The relationship creates a foundation for Vultr and SoftwareOne to explore cloud optimization, workload performance, cloud economics, and greater choice for enterprise customers, helping enterprises get greater value from existing and future cloud investments.

...

Vultr and SoftwareOne see an opportunity to give enterprises greater infrastructure choice, enabling them to optimize their cloud estates for enhanced performance and cost efficiencies. This is particularly relevant for modern, portable workloads where performance, economics, and architectural flexibility are important considerations.

Vultr VX1 Cloud Compute represents one area of alignment, combining x86 compatibility with leading price-to-performance. VX1 allows enterprises to improve workload performance and cloud economics while maintaining familiar x86 architecture and avoiding unnecessary application rearchitecture.

...

“Enterprise cloud strategies increasingly require greater choice across infrastructure, performance, and economics. With VX1 Cloud Compute, Vultr provides x86 infrastructure designed for leading price-to-performance and strong cloud economics, alongside Vultr Cloud GPU for demanding AI workloads. SoftwareOne brings deep expertise in cloud optimization and FinOps, helping enterprises make more informed infrastructure decisions based on workload requirements.”

— Kevin Cochrane, CMO, Vultr

results.title: Run Your Own Inference Stack on Vultr with Modelplane | Vultr Blogs
highlights:
# Run Your Own Inference Stack on Vultr with Modelplane

2 min read September 3, 2026 0

Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE) is now a supported inference cluster provider in Modelplane, the open source control plane for AI models. As of the v0.3 release, you can describe a GPU cluster on Vultr in a short YAML manifest. You specify the region, node pool, instance class, and the minimum and maximum node counts you want it to scale between, and Modelplane has the full serving stack stood up for you: VPC, control plane, system and GPU node pools, and the inference layer on top.

results.title: Accelerate OpenFold3 with AMD and Vultr | Vultr Blogs
highlights:
# Accelerate OpenFold3 with AMD and Vultr

1 min read September 14, 2026 0

AI is transforming drug discovery and life sciences, but deploying production-ready AI models can introduce significant infrastructure complexity. OpenFold3 helps researchers predict the 3D structures of proteins, antibodies, DNA, RNA, protein complexes, and small-molecule ligands – but putting these capabilities into production requires the right platform and infrastructure.

MindWalk independently validated AMD Inference Microservices (AIM) for OpenFold3 on Vultr Kubernetes Engine (VKE), powered by AMD Instinct MI325X GPUs. The validation demonstrates how a standardized, Kubernetes-native platform can simplify deployment for demanding protein structure prediction workflows.

With AMD AIM for OpenFold3 available through the VKE Marketplace, researchers can streamline deployment, networking, HTTPS configuration, and model serving without having to manually assemble the underlying infrastructure.
